case_name: Smt. Rachna Jain vs Shri Neeraj Jain
facts_of_case: Marriage between the petitioner/wife and respondent/husband was solemnized on 12.3.1996. The wife was subjected to cruelty and humiliation by the husband, who demanded dowry and cash. The parties have been living separately since 7th Feb.2002.

legal_principles.principle: A party to a petition under Section 13B of the Hindu Marriage Act can unilaterally withdraw his/her consent before the passing of the decree.
legal_principles.held: Although later on in the case of Ashok Hura v. Rupa Bipin Zeveri reported as I (1997) DMC 491 (SC) = AIR 1997 SC page 1266, the Hon'ble Supreme Court observed that the decision in the case of Sureshta Devi v. Om Prakash requires reconsideration because the observations made therein about the time limit for withdrawal of the consent is too wide and that question what left open
cited_cases: Sureshta Devi v. Om Prakash (1991) DMC 313 (SC) = AIR 1992 SC 1904
Ashok Hura v. Rupa Bipin Zeveri reported as I (1997) DMC 491 (SC) = AIR 1997 SC page 1266

legal_principles.principle: The consent given in the first motion petition under Section 13(B)(1) of the Hindu Marriage Act is irrevocable and can be unilaterally withdrawn by either party before the passing of the decree.
legal_principles.held: has been held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sureshta Devi v. Om Prakash (supra)
cited_cases: Sureshta Devi v. Om Prakash (1991) DMC 313 (SC) = AIR 1992 SC 1904

outcome.final_order: The Additional District Judge has declined to grant divorce to the petitioner/wife by permitting the unilateral withdrawal of mutual consent by the respondent/husband.
